schedule.name: Adult: HIV infection
schedule.description: HIV infection. Applies on top of the adult age schedule only for patients a clinician has put on it; its rules replace the age rule for the same vaccine.

rules.why_text: CDC adult schedule 2025, HIV infection: age 19 or older, 2 doses of recombinant zoster vaccine 2 to 6 months apart (minimum 4 weeks)
CDC adult schedule 2025, HIV infection: through age 26, complete a 3-dose series even if it was started at 9 to 14
CDC adult schedule 2025, HIV infection: 2-dose HepA series (Havrix 6 to 12 months apart, Vaqta 6 to 18), or 3-dose HepA-HepB (Twinrix)

rules.review_reason: Hepatitis B: 2, 3 or 4 doses depending on the vaccine used (2 doses for Heplisav-B). Dialysis uses the dialysis formulation. Check the series.
rules.why_text: CDC adult schedule 2025, HIV infection: HIV infection is a hepatitis B risk factor: complete the series

rules.review_reason: Pneumococcal: choose PCV15 (then PPSV23 at least 1 year later; 8 weeks if immunocompromised), PCV20 or PCV21. Check earlier PCV13 and PPSV23 doses first.
rules.why_text: CDC adult schedule 2025, HIV infection: age 19 or older, 1 dose of PCV15, PCV20 or PCV21 if no earlier conjugate vaccine

CDC adult schedule 2025, HIV infection: 2-dose primary series (Menveo or MenQuadfi) at least 8 weeks apart. Booster 5 years after the primary series and every 5 years while risk remains (not tracked yet)

rules.review_reason: HIV: MMR only if CD4 is 15% or more and 200 cells/mm3 or more for at least 6 months (2 doses at least 4 weeks apart). Contraindicated otherwise.
rules.why_text: CDC adult schedule 2025, HIV infection: MMR depends on CD4 count

rules.review_reason: HIV: varicella vaccine may be considered only if CD4 is 15% or more and 200 cells/mm3 or more (2 doses 3 months apart). Contraindicated otherwise.
rules.why_text: CDC adult schedule 2025, HIV infection: varicella depends on CD4 count
